steps.narration: Factoring turns a quadratic into two brackets multiplied together. If their product is zero, at least one bracket must be zero.
For question 3, first make the equation simpler. Every term is divisible by 2, so divide both sides by 2.
To factor this, find two numbers whose product is 3 and whose sum is −4. Those numbers are −1 and −3.

elements.why: Product = constant; sum = coefficient of x

steps.narration: Use those numbers to make the brackets. Expanding them gives x squared minus 3x minus x plus 3, exactly what we need.
Now apply the zero-product rule: set each bracket equal to zero. This gives two solutions!

elements.why: At least one factor must be zero

steps.narration: Check both answers in the original equation. Both make the left side zero, so both work.
